title: What can you say about black cohosh in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for black cohosh; the strongest is "Used in herbal medicine to help relieve premenstrual symptoms" (moderate, 40-2,400 mg dried root a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats menopause, or replaces hormone therapy (HRT)".

supported_wordings.wording: Used in herbal medicine to help relieve symptoms associated with menopause.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it, but ODS reports trials and guidelines that do not show it works for hot flashes.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 40-2,400 mg of dried root and/or rhizome a day, as dried herb or an ethanol or water extract.
supported_wordings.form: Dried root and/or rhizome, or its ethanol or water extract

sources.name: NIH ODS fact sheet: Black Cohosh (health professional)

supported_wordings.where_sources_disagree: Health Canada lists this use at 40-2,400 mg dried root a day. ODS reports that a review found no significant reduction in hot flashes and other vasomotor symptoms, and that the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists concluded in 2015 that the data do not show herbal supplements such as black cohosh work for them.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
